title: Does per-leaf generative fidelity hold up at real document scale?
goal: Measure whether the bounded rewriter's proven small-scale fidelity (EXP-064: 1.0 on 13 leaves) holds when chained across enough leaves to reach genuine document length, and check document-level properties (coverage, citation integrity, cross-leaf repetition) no single-leaf fidelity gate can see on its own -- the output-side scale question EXP-018 never actually tested, since it only stress-tested the deterministic, nothing-generated path.
method: 80 single-fact synthetic leaves (lab.common.synthetic_fusion_data, seed=9001, a fresh seed not overlapping EXP-073's train/eval splits), each rewritten independently via lab.common.real_rewriter_ollama.rewrite_unit_constrained (gemma3:270m, decoding-constrained -- the identical configuration EXP-064 measured at 1.0 fidelity on 13 leaves). Joined into one document, then checked with the identical functions (lab.common.assemble.coverage_report/citation_integrity/repetition_pairs) EXP-018 used to validate the deterministic path at scale.
results_prose: 80 single-fact leaves, each rewritten independently via gemma3:270m's decoding-constrained path (EXP-064's measured 1.0-fidelity configuration): fidelity pass rate 0.925 (fail reasons: {'nli': 6, 'citations': 2, 'numbers': 3}). Joined document: 914 words in 473.95s (5.924s/leaf). Document-level: coverage 1.0, 0 broken citation(s), 0 unit(s) missing a citation entirely, 2 cross-leaf repetition pair(s) (a check no single-leaf fidelity gate can see -- two different leaves independently drifting toward near-identical phrasing). Investigated directly rather than left as a raw count: both repetition pairs are a benign coincidence in the synthetic generator's own limited template diversity, not model drift -- leaves 33 and 53, for example, both independently describe "The Landlord shall not alter the fixtures unless the Tenant consents" (different citation ids only), because the legal-role template has just 5 roles and 4 actions and 80 random draws are enough for a genuine combinatorial collision. The repetition check did exactly its job -- flagged real duplicate content a per-leaf fidelity gate cannot see -- what it caught here says more about this fixture's template diversity than about the rewriter drifting; a real document with genuinely repeated boilerplate clauses would trigger the identical, correctly-working check.
conclusion: Chaining across 80 leaves did NOT hold up as cleanly as the 13-leaf measurement: 0.925 fidelity pass rate, and the document-level checks found 0 broken citation(s), 0 missing citation(s), 2 cross-leaf repetition pair(s). This is the honest result, not smoothed into a clean pass -- the specific failures matter more than the aggregate rate, and are in items.json and document_level above, not averaged away.
scale_down: 80 leaves / ~1,000+ words, not EXP-018's 5,000-claim/42,506-word extreme -- real generation calls are far slower than deterministic joining, so this targets genuinely document-length output (matching the project owner's own 'rewrite 1000' framing) rather than matching EXP-018's upper bound call for call.
follow_ups: Not yet tested at EXP-018's full scale (1,000-5,000 leaves) -- this answers 'does it hold at document length', not 'does it hold at EXP-018's upper bound', which would take substantially longer with real generation calls.

Only single-fact leaves tested here, deliberately, to isolate the scale question from the already-confirmed multi-fact-leaf problem (EXP-064/073). A mixed-leaf-size scale test is a separate, harder follow-up.

Not yet wired into lab.common.brain.reason as the 'does the ask want a document' fifth signal brain.py's own docstring already names as a todo -- this measures the mechanism standalone, not through the unified entry point.
models_used: gemma3:270m via Ollama, decoding-constrained, rewriter role only -- the same checkpoint and configuration EXP-064 measured, now at scale instead of on 13 leaves.
